entries.subject: Vara-Lubiano et al. (2022) 2019 occultation and light-curve solution
entries.finding: The selected shape is the published triaxial interpretation with semiaxes 339 +/-5, 235 +/-6 and 226 +/-8 km from the observed light-curve amplitude and the original occultation chords; it is not a homogeneous Jacobi-equilibrium figure and the smooth model reproduces no local terrain.

entries.subject: Alternative aligned-chord scenarios in the same paper
entries.finding: The README records that the observed-amplitude solution using the original chords was selected rather than the paper's alternative aligned-chord scenarios.
entries.revisitWhen: A later analysis prefers an aligned-chord scenario over the observed-amplitude solution.

entries.subject: Older 2019 shape fit
entries.finding: The older 2019 fit used a lower light-curve amplitude and the 2022 work explains why it is superseded, so it is not used.
entries.revisitWhen: A new analysis reinstates the lower light-curve amplitude or supersedes the 2022 solution.

entries.subject: Published model-derived ecliptic pole
entries.finding: The display uses the paper's model-derived ecliptic pole at longitude 228 degrees and latitude 39 degrees, converted with J2000 mean obliquity 23.439291111 degrees.

entries.subject: Pole equinox, aspect ambiguity and uncertainty
entries.finding: The README records that J2000 is assumed because the paper does not specify an equinox, and that the 59/121 degree aspect ambiguity and the unquoted pole uncertainty remain, with an arbitrary prime meridian and rotational phase.
entries.revisitWhen: The authors or a later publication state the pole equinox, resolve the aspect ambiguity or quote a pole uncertainty.

entries.subject: JPL Horizons elements and independent vectors
entries.finding: Retained Horizons elements, cross-checked against independent vectors, give the heliocentric geometric position at the fixed 2026-09-03 epoch; the fixed-epoch two-body orbit does not simulate long-term perturbations.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: No resolved global imagery is available in these source products, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-coverage grid and the normal grid marks unmapped terrain with Shadows off by default.
